record.paper_title: Recent advances and open questions on the susy structure of the chiral de Rham Complex
record.context_brief: Direct Hamiltonian-reduction construction of CDR supersymmetries
record.original_question: Can the supersymmetry algebras inside the chiral de Rham complex of special-holonomy manifolds be constructed directly by quantum Hamiltonian reduction: specifically, is there a morphism from the BRST complex C^•(g, f) defining W_k(g, f) to Ω_ch(M), or to a resolution of Ω_ch(M), that induces the N=2, N=4, SV^Spin7, and SV^G2 embeddings described geometrically?

evidence.quote: The connection between the quantum Hamiltonian reduction and the chiral de Rham complex ΩchM remains a mystery to this day.
All of the supersymmetry algebras of the chiral de Rham complex discussed in the previous section are W algebras.

1 Question. Can one construct the supersymmetries of the chiral de Rham complex directly by Hamiltonian reduction, namely, is there a morphism from C•(g, f) to either ΩchM or perhaps a resolution, inducing the embeddings described in the previous section?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let M be a smooth Riemannian manifold with special holonomy (in particular, of holonomy type SU(n), Sp(n), Spin(7), or G_2), and let Ω^{ch}_M denote its chiral de Rham complex, the sheaf of vertex superalgebras canonically attached to M. It is known that, depending on the holonomy, the vertex algebra of global sections of Ω^{ch}_M contains a distinguished superconformal subalgebra: an N=2 superconformal algebra (Calabi–Yau case), an N=4 superconformal algebra (hyperkähler case), the Shatashvili–Vafa Spin(7) algebra SV^{Spin(7)}, or the Shatashvili–Vafa G_2 algebra SV^{G_2}.

Each of these superconformal algebras is also known to arise as a quantum W-algebra W_k(g,f) obtained by quantum Hamiltonian (Drinfeld–Sokolov / BRST) reduction of an affine vertex superalgebra associated with a suitable Lie superalgebra g and nilpotent element f, computed as the cohomology of an explicit BRST complex C^•(g,f).

Question: Does there exist a morphism of complexes (compatible with the vertex algebra structure)
   φ : C^•(g,f) ⟶ Ω^{ch}_M
or, more generally, a morphism from C^•(g,f) into a resolution of Ω^{ch}_M, such that the induced map on cohomology realizes the geometric embeddings of the N=2, N=4, SV^{Spin(7)}, and SV^{G_2} algebras into the chiral de Rham complex of M? Equivalently, can the supersymmetry algebras of Ω^{ch}_M for special-holonomy manifolds be constructed directly by quantum Hamiltonian reduction?
artifact.status_search_result: A search of the literature on the chiral de Rham complex, Hamiltonian reduction, and Shatashvili–Vafa / Odake algebras (including subsequent work on G_2 manifolds being superconformal) shows that while the relevant superconformal algebras are recognized as W-algebras and the geometric embeddings are constructed by direct vertex-algebraic methods, no morphism from the BRST complex C^•(g,f) into Ω^{ch}_M (or a resolution) inducing these embeddings has been exhibited. The connection between quantum Hamiltonian reduction and the chiral de Rham complex is described as still mysterious, and no later resolution of this question was found.

status_evidence.title: Recent advances and open questions on the susy structure of the chiral de Rham Complex
status_evidence.snippet: Lists the question of constructing CDR supersymmetries directly via Hamiltonian reduction as an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The question is posed as open.

status_evidence.title: G2 Holonomy Manifolds are Superconformal
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs commuting copies of the Shatashvili–Vafa G2 algebra inside the CDR by direct geometric/vertex-algebra methods, not via a BRST morphism from C^•(g,f).
status_evidence.claim: Embeddings are achieved geometrically rather than via Hamiltonian reduction.

status_evidence.title: Chiral de Rham complex on Riemannian manifolds and special holonomy
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes N=1, N=2, N=4 and special holonomy superconformal structures on CDR via superfield formalism.
status_evidence.claim: Existing constructions of these embeddings do not use Hamiltonian reduction.
